subproblem.title: Coordinates, linearity, norm and inner product of graphPoint
subproblem.statement: For all n, l >= 0, let Amb n l = R^(n+l) (EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n + l))) and, for a in R^n and b in R^l, let graphPoint(a, b) := toLp(Fin.append a b) be the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of a and whose last l coordinates are those of b. Then: (C1) for all a in R^n, b in R^l and i in Fin n, the coordinate of graphPoint(a, b) at castAdd l i is a_i; (C2) for all a in R^n, b in R^l and j in Fin l, the coordinate of graphPoint(a, b) at natAdd n j is b_j; and for all a, a' in R^n, b, b' in R^l and t in R: (L1) graphPoint(a + a', b + b') = graphPoint(a, b) + graphPoint(a', b'); (L2) graphPoint(a - a', b - b') = graphPoint(a, b) - graphPoint(a', b'); (L3) graphPoint(t a, t b) = t graphPoint(a, b); (L4) |graphPoint(a, b)|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2; (IP) <graphPoint(a, b), graphPoint(a', b')> = <a, a'> + <b, b'> (real Euclidean inner products of R^(n+l), R^n and R^l).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ) (i : Fin n), graphPoint a b (Fin.castAdd ℓ i) = a i) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ) (j : Fin ℓ), graphPoint a b (Fin.natAdd n j) = b j) ∧ (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (a + a') (b + b') = graphPoint a b + graphPoint a' b') ∧ (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (a - a') (b - b') = graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (t • a) (t • b) = t • graphPoint a b) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), ‖graphPoint a b‖ ^ 2 = ‖a‖ ^ 2 + ‖b‖ ^ 2) ∧ (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), inner ℝ (graphPoint a b) (graphPoint a' b') = inner ℝ a a' + inner ℝ b b')
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. N := n + l. For x in R^N = Amb n l and k in Fin N, x_k is the k-th coordinate of x; similarly for vectors of R^n and R^l. By definition graphPoint a b = toLp(Fin.append a b), the vector of R^N whose coordinate function is Fin.append (coordinates of a) (coordinates of b).

1. Index decomposition. Every k in Fin N is of one of the forms castAdd l i with i in Fin n (value i < n) or natAdd n j with j in Fin l (value n + j >= n) (Fin.addCases). The maps castAdd l and natAdd n are injective, and castAdd l i is never equal to natAdd n j, because their values satisfy i < n <= n + j.

2. (C1), (C2). Fin.append evaluates at castAdd l i to the i-th entry of its first argument and at natAdd n j to the j-th entry of its second argument (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right), and the coordinates of toLp f are the values of f. Hence (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} = a_i and (graphPoint a b)_{natAdd n j} = b_j.

3. Extensionality. Two vectors of R^N are equal if and only if their coordinates agree at every k in Fin N, and by step 1 it suffices to compare them at every castAdd l i (i in Fin n) and at every natAdd n j (j in Fin l). Sums, differences and scalar multiples in R^N, R^n and R^l are computed coordinatewise.

4. (L1). At castAdd l i the left side has coordinate (a + a')_i = a_i + a'_i by (C1), and the right side has coordinate (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} + (graphPoint a' b')_{castAdd l i} = a_i + a'_i by (C1). At natAdd n j both sides have coordinate b_j + b'_j by (C2). By step 3 the two vectors are equal.

5. (L2). Exactly as in step 4 with differences: at castAdd l i both coordinates are a_i - a'_i, and at natAdd n j both are b_j - b'_j, by (C1), (C2).

6. (L3). Exactly as in step 4 with scalar multiples: at castAdd l i both coordinates are t a_i, and at natAdd n j both are t b_j, by (C1), (C2).

7. (L4). In the Euclidean space R^N, |x|^2 = sum_{k in Fin N} x_k^2 (EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq; for reals |x_k|^2 = x_k^2), and likewise |a|^2 = sum_{i in Fin n} a_i^2 in R^n and |b|^2 = sum_{j in Fin l} b_j^2 in R^l. A sum over Fin (n + l) equals the sum over i in Fin n of the term at castAdd l i plus the sum over j in Fin l of the term at natAdd n j (Fin.sum_univ_add, which is the bijection of step 1). Applying this to x = graphPoint a b and using (C1), (C2): |graphPoint a b|^2 = sum_{i} a_i^2 + sum_{j} b_j^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2.

8. (IP). The real inner product of R^N is <x, y> = sum_{k in Fin N} x_k y_k (PiLp.inner_apply; for real scalars the summand <x_k, y_k> is the product x_k y_k), and likewise in R^n and R^l. Splitting the sum as in step 7 and using (C1), (C2) for both graphPoint a b and graphPoint a' b': <graphPoint a b, graphPoint a' b'> = sum_{i} a_i a'_i + sum_{j} b_j b'_j = <a, a'> + <b, b'>.

Every step is valid for all n, l >= 0: if n = 0 or l = 0, the corresponding index case of step 1 does not occur and the corresponding sums are empty.
proof_key_steps: Every index of Fin (n+l) is exactly one of castAdd l i or natAdd n j, and Fin.append gives the coordinates a_i and b_j there: (C1), (C2)
(L1)-(L3) by comparing coordinates at both kinds of indices (extensionality in R^(n+l))
(L4) and (IP) by splitting the coordinate sums |x|^2 = sum_k x_k^2 and <x,y> = sum_k x_k y_k with Fin.sum_univ_add and applying (C1), (C2)

audit.reason: The proposition matches C1, C2, L1–L4 and IP with all quantifiers present. Steps 1–3 establish exhaustive coordinate decomposition, append evaluation and extensionality; steps 4–6 prove the linearity identities; steps 7–8 split the Euclidean norm and inner-product sums. Empty index types are covered. The proof is complete and non-circular. Its additional coordinate and inner-product conclusions genuinely support rotated_plane.

subproblem.title: Hilbert-Schmidt norm basics and the Hilbert-Schmidt bound for orthogonal projections
subproblem.statement: (L8) For all m, k >= 0 and all continuous linear maps M, N : R^m -> R^k, with hsNormSq M := sum_{i in Fin m} |M e_i|^2 (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 the standard basis of R^m), hsNorm M := sqrt(hsNormSq M) and ||M|| the operator norm: (a) 0 <= hsNormSq M; (b) hsNorm(M)^2 = hsNormSq M; (c) hsNormSq(M + N) <= 2 hsNormSq M + 2 hsNormSq N; (d) hsNormSq(-M) = hsNormSq M; (e) hsNormSq M = 0 implies M = 0; (f) ||M|| <= hsNorm M; (g) hsNorm M <= sqrt(m) ||M||. (L9) For every m >= 0 and every linear subspace K of R^m, with P_K := K.starProjection the orthogonal projection onto K viewed as a continuous linear map R^m -> R^m, hsNormSq(P_K) <= m.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (m k : ℕ) (M N : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k), 0 ≤ hsNormSq M ∧ hsNorm M ^ 2 = hsNormSq M ∧ hsNormSq (M + N) ≤ 2 * hsNormSq M + 2 * hsNormSq N ∧ hsNormSq (-M) = hsNormSq M ∧ (hsNormSq M = 0 → M = 0) ∧ ‖M‖ ≤ hsNorm M ∧ hsNorm M ≤ Real.sqrt m * ‖M‖) ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (K : Submodule ℝ (Rn m)), hsNormSq K.starProjection ≤ m
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. e_i (i in Fin m) is the standard basis of R^m (EuclideanSpace.single i 1); |e_i| = 1, every v in R^m equals sum_i v_i e_i, and |v|^2 = sum_i v_i^2. hsNormSq M = sum_{i in Fin m} |M e_i|^2 and hsNorm M = sqrt(hsNormSq M). The operator norm satisfies |M v| <= ||M|| |v| for all v (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm), and if C >= 0 and |M v| <= C |v| for all v then ||M|| <= C (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound).

1. (a). Each summand |M e_i|^2 is >= 0, so the finite sum hsNormSq M is >= 0.

2. (b). By (a), hsNormSq M >= 0, so hsNorm(M)^2 = (sqrt(hsNormSq M))^2 = hsNormSq M.

3. (c). Fix i and put x := |M e_i| >= 0, y := |N e_i| >= 0 and z := |(M + N) e_i| = |M e_i + N e_i| >= 0. By the triangle inequality 0 <= z <= x + y, hence z^2 <= (x + y)^2. Moreover (x + y)^2 <= 2x^2 + 2y^2, because 2x^2 + 2y^2 - (x + y)^2 = (x - y)^2 >= 0. Thus |(M + N) e_i|^2 <= 2|M e_i|^2 + 2|N e_i|^2 for every i, and summing over i in Fin m gives hsNormSq(M + N) <= 2 hsNormSq M + 2 hsNormSq N.

4. (d). For every i, |(-M) e_i| = |-(M e_i)| = |M e_i|, so the two sums agree term by term.

5. (e). Suppose hsNormSq M = 0. A finite sum of nonnegative terms is 0 only if every term is 0 (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg), so |M e_i|^2 = 0 and hence M e_i = 0 for every i. For any v in R^m, v = sum_i v_i e_i, so by linearity M v = sum_i v_i M e_i = 0. Two continuous linear maps that agree at every vector are equal, so M = 0. (For m = 0, R^m = {0} and the same argument applies with empty sums.)

6. (f). Let v be in R^m. By linearity and the triangle inequality, |M v| = |sum_i v_i M e_i| <= sum_i |v_i| |M e_i|. By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for finite sums (Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq), (sum_i |v_i| |M e_i|)^2 <= (sum_i |v_i|^2)(sum_i |M e_i|^2) = |v|^2 hsNormSq M. Since 0 <= |M v| <= sum_i |v_i| |M e_i|, squaring gives |M v|^2 <= hsNormSq M |v|^2 = (hsNorm M |v|)^2 by (b); as |M v| >= 0 and hsNorm M |v| >= 0, it follows that |M v| <= hsNorm M |v|. Since hsNorm M = sqrt(hsNormSq M) >= 0, the operator-norm bound gives ||M|| <= hsNorm M.

7. (g). For each i, |M e_i| <= ||M|| |e_i| = ||M||, and both sides are >= 0, so |M e_i|^2 <= ||M||^2. Summing over the m indices, hsNormSq M <= m ||M||^2. The square root is monotone, so hsNorm M = sqrt(hsNormSq M) <= sqrt(m ||M||^2) = sqrt(m) sqrt(||M||^2) = sqrt(m) ||M||, using m >= 0 and ||M|| >= 0.

8. (L9). K is a subspace of the finite-dimensional space R^m, hence finite-dimensional and complete, so its orthogonal projection P_K exists, with P_K v in K and v - P_K v orthogonal to K for every v. By Pythagoras, |v|^2 = |P_K v + (v - P_K v)|^2 = |P_K v|^2 + |v - P_K v|^2 >= |P_K v|^2, so |P_K v| <= |v| (Mathlib: Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le). For v = e_i this gives |P_K e_i|^2 <= |e_i|^2 = 1, and summing over the m indices, hsNormSq(P_K) = sum_{i in Fin m} |P_K e_i|^2 <= m.

Every step is valid for all m, k >= 0: for m = 0 all sums over Fin m are empty, so hsNormSq M = hsNormSq N = hsNormSq(M + N) = hsNorm M = 0 = m, and R^0 = {0} forces M = 0 and ||M|| = 0, so every clause reduces to an (in)equality between zeros or to M = 0; for k = 0 every vector of R^k is 0, so all quantities |M e_i|, |M v|, hsNormSq M and ||M|| vanish and the inequalities hold trivially (the general argument above covers these cases as well).
proof_key_steps: (a), (b), (d) termwise from the definition; (c) from the triangle inequality and (x + y)^2 <= 2x^2 + 2y^2 at each basis vector
(e): every |M e_i| vanishes, so M vanishes on the expansion v = sum_i v_i e_i
(f): |M v| <= sum_i |v_i||M e_i| <= |v| hsNorm M by Cauchy-Schwarz, then the operator-norm bound
(g): |M e_i| <= ||M|| gives hsNormSq M <= m ||M||^2; take square roots
(L9): |P_K e_i| <= |e_i| = 1 by Pythagoras; sum over the m basis vectors

audit.reason: The proposition exactly matches L8(a–g) and L9. Steps 1–5 correctly use nonnegative finite sums, square roots, triangle inequalities, negation and basis expansion. Step 6 derives the pointwise Cauchy–Schwarz bound before applying the operator-norm criterion with a nonnegative constant. Step 7 justifies squaring and taking square roots. Step 8 obtains projection contraction from finite-dimensional completeness and Pythagoras, then sums over the basis. The proof is independent, non-circular and complete, including dimensions zero.

subproblem.title: Projection onto, distance to, and dimension of the rotated plane T_0 = q(R^n x {0})
subproblem.statement: For all n, l >= 0 and every linear isometric equivalence q of R^(n+l) = Amb n l onto itself: let graphPoint(a, b) be the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of a in R^n and whose last l coordinates are those of b in R^l, horizontalPlane := span{eps_{castAdd l i} : i in Fin n} (eps_k the standard basis vectors of R^(n+l)), T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane) (the image of horizontalPlane under the linear map underlying q) and P_{T_0} := (rotatedPlane q).starProjection its orthogonal projection. Then (L5) P_{T_0}(q(graphPoint(a, b))) = q(graphPoint(a, 0)) for all a in R^n, b in R^l; (L6) infDist(q(graphPoint(a, b)), T_0) = |b| for all a in R^n, b in R^l; (L7) finrank T_0 = n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), (rotatedPlane q).starProjection (q (graphPoint a b)) = q (graphPoint a (0 : Rn ℓ))) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), infDist (q (graphPoint a b)) (rotatedPlane q : Set (Amb n ℓ)) = ‖b‖) ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (rotatedPlane q) = n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. N := n + l; eps_k (k in Fin N) are the standard basis vectors of R^N = Amb n l and e_i (i in Fin n) those of R^n. horizontalPlane = span{eps_{castAdd l i} : i in Fin n}, and T_0 = rotatedPlane q = {q(h) : h in horizontalPlane}. From the sibling theorem graph_coords (Submission.any_radius_gr_la_graphPoint_algebra) at n, l we use: (C1) for all a in R^n, b in R^l and i in Fin n, (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} = a_i; (C2) for all a in R^n, b in R^l and j in Fin l, (graphPoint a b)_{natAdd n j} = b_j; and for all a, a' in R^n, b, b' in R^l and t in R: (L1) graphPoint(a + a', b + b') = graphPoint a b + graphPoint a' b'; (L2) graphPoint(a - a', b - b') = graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b'; (L3) graphPoint(t a, t b) = t graphPoint a b; (L4) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2; (IP) <graphPoint a b, graphPoint a' b'> = <a, a'> + <b, b'>.

1. eps_{castAdd l i} = graphPoint(e_i, 0) for every i in Fin n. Compare coordinates; every index of Fin N is castAdd l i' (i' in Fin n) or natAdd n j (j in Fin l) (Fin.addCases). At castAdd l i' the left side is 1 if castAdd l i' = castAdd l i, i.e. i' = i (castAdd l is injective, Fin.castAdd_injective), and 0 otherwise; the right side is (e_i)_{i'} by (C1), which is also 1 if i' = i and 0 otherwise. At natAdd n j the left side is 0, because natAdd n j is not castAdd l i (their values satisfy n + j >= n > i); the right side is the j-th coordinate of 0 in R^l, i.e. 0, by (C2).

2. The map G : R^n -> R^N, G(c) := graphPoint(c, 0), is linear: G(c + c') = graphPoint(c + c', 0 + 0) = G(c) + G(c') by (L1), and G(t c) = graphPoint(t c, t 0) = t G(c) by (L3), using 0 + 0 = 0 and t 0 = 0 in R^l.

3. horizontalPlane = {graphPoint(c, 0) : c in R^n}.
(a) For c in R^n write c = sum_i c_i e_i. By step 2 and step 1, graphPoint(c, 0) = G(c) = sum_i c_i G(e_i) = sum_i c_i eps_{castAdd l i}, a linear combination of the spanning vectors; hence graphPoint(c, 0) lies in horizontalPlane.
(b) Every h in horizontalPlane, the span of the finite family (eps_{castAdd l i})_{i in Fin n}, is a linear combination h = sum_i c_i eps_{castAdd l i} for some reals c_i (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). By step 1 and step 2, h = sum_i c_i G(e_i) = G(sum_i c_i e_i) = graphPoint(sum_i c_i e_i, 0).
(For n = 0 both sets are {0}: the span of the empty family is {0}, and the empty sums give h = 0 = G(0).)

4. Orthogonality. For every b in R^l and every h in horizontalPlane, <graphPoint(0, b), h> = 0: by step 3(b), h = graphPoint(c, 0) for some c in R^n, and by (IP), <graphPoint(0, b), graphPoint(c, 0)> = <0, c> + <b, 0> = 0 + 0 = 0.

5. q preserves inner products: <q x, q y> = <x, y> for all x, y in R^N. Indeed q is linear and preserves norms, so by the polarization identity 4<x, y> = |x + y|^2 - |x - y|^2 we get 4<q x, q y> = |q(x + y)|^2 - |q(x - y)|^2 = |x + y|^2 - |x - y|^2 = 4<x, y> (Mathlib: LinearIsometryEquiv.inner_map_map).

6. (L5). Fix a in R^n, b in R^l and put v := q(graphPoint(a, b)), k := q(graphPoint(a, 0)).
(i) k lies in T_0, because graphPoint(a, 0) lies in horizontalPlane by step 3(a).
(ii) v - k = q(graphPoint(a, b) - graphPoint(a, 0)) by linearity of q, and graphPoint(a, b) - graphPoint(a, 0) = graphPoint(a - a, b - 0) = graphPoint(0, b) by (L2); so v - k = q(graphPoint(0, b)).
(iii) Every w in T_0 is w = q(h) with h in horizontalPlane, and <v - k, w> = <q(graphPoint(0, b)), q(h)> = <graphPoint(0, b), h> = 0 by (ii), step 5 and step 4.
(iv) T_0 is a subspace of the finite-dimensional space R^N, hence finite-dimensional and complete, so its orthogonal projection P_{T_0} exists; P_{T_0} v lies in T_0 and v - P_{T_0} v is orthogonal to T_0. Characterization: if k lies in T_0 and <v - k, w> = 0 for all w in T_0, then P_{T_0} v = k. Proof: d := P_{T_0} v - k lies in T_0, and d = (v - k) - (v - P_{T_0} v), so |d|^2 = <v - k, d> - <v - P_{T_0} v, d> = 0 - 0 = 0, whence d = 0 (Mathlib: Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero).
By (i), (iii) and (iv), P_{T_0}(q(graphPoint(a, b))) = q(graphPoint(a, 0)).

7. Distance to a complete subspace. Let K be a complete subspace of R^N with orthogonal projection P := P_K, and let v be in R^N. For every k in K, v - Pv is orthogonal to K and Pv - k lies in K, so by Pythagoras |v - k|^2 = |(v - Pv) + (Pv - k)|^2 = |v - Pv|^2 + |Pv - k|^2 >= |v - Pv|^2, i.e. |v - k| >= |v - Pv|. Since Pv itself lies in K, the infimum infDist(v, K) = inf_{k in K} |v - k| equals |v - Pv| = dist(v, Pv) (Mathlib: Submodule.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist).

8. (L6). Fix a, b and let v := q(graphPoint(a, b)). By step 7 with K = T_0 (complete by step 6(iv)) and by (L5) from step 6, infDist(v, T_0) = |v - P_{T_0} v| = |q(graphPoint(a, b)) - q(graphPoint(a, 0))| = |q(graphPoint(0, b))| by step 6(ii), and this equals |graphPoint(0, b)| because q is an isometry. By (L4), |graphPoint(0, b)|^2 = |0|^2 + |b|^2 = |b|^2, and both norms are >= 0, so |graphPoint(0, b)| = |b|. Hence infDist(q(graphPoint(a, b)), T_0) = |b|.

9. (L7). The standard basis (eps_k)_{k in Fin N} is orthonormal (EuclideanSpace.orthonormal_single), hence linearly independent; composing with the injective map castAdd l : Fin n -> Fin N (Fin.castAdd_injective; LinearIndependent.comp), the family (eps_{castAdd l i})_{i in Fin n} is linearly independent. The span of a linearly independent family indexed by a finite type has finrank equal to the number of indices (finrank_span_eq_card), so finrank horizontalPlane = card(Fin n) = n. T_0 is the image of horizontalPlane under the linear equivalence underlying q, which restricts to a linear isomorphism from horizontalPlane onto T_0; linear isomorphisms preserve finrank (LinearEquiv.finrank_map_eq). Hence finrank T_0 = n.

Every step is valid for all n, l >= 0, including n = 0 (where horizontalPlane = T_0 = {0}, finrank 0) and l = 0.
proof_key_steps: eps_{castAdd l i} = graphPoint(e_i, 0) by coordinates (C1), (C2); c -> graphPoint(c, 0) is linear by (L1), (L3); hence horizontalPlane = {graphPoint(c, 0) : c in R^n}
(IP) gives <graphPoint(0, b), graphPoint(c, 0)> = 0, so graphPoint(0, b) is orthogonal to horizontalPlane; the linear isometry q preserves inner products
q(graphPoint(a, 0)) lies in T_0 and q(graphPoint(a, b)) - q(graphPoint(a, 0)) = q(graphPoint(0, b)) (by (L2)) is orthogonal to T_0, so the characterization of the orthogonal projection gives (L5)
Pythagoras gives infDist(v, K) = |v - P_K v| for complete K; with (L5), the isometry q and (L4) this is |graphPoint(0, b)| = |b| (L6)
The standard basis vectors at the distinct indices castAdd l i are orthonormal, hence independent, so finrank horizontalPlane = n, preserved by the linear equivalence q (L7)

audit.reason: The proposition exactly states L5–L7 for the specified linear isometric equivalence. Steps 1–4 derive the horizontal-plane description and vertical orthogonality using only graph_coords. Steps 5–6 establish projection membership, orthogonal residual and uniqueness, with completeness justified. Steps 7–8 establish the attained distance minimum and the norm equality with explicit nonnegativity. Step 9 proves dimension using an independent coordinate family and preservation under linear equivalence. Zero-dimensional cases remain valid; the dependency is correctly directed and non-circular.
